keyPoints: The product must be accessible to all age groups with a fashionable, trendy aesthetic.
The control should be uncluttered, easy to find, and not easily lost with low-cost cues.
A flip-open design with an electronic panel is proposed to reduce size and add features.
The control is limited to TV and video, not combined controls, to simplify use and cost.
Ergonomics must adapt to different country sizes with potential for larger or smaller controls.
A touch-screen interface is considered as a wear-resistant alternative for younger, office users.
The remote should avoid generic designs and have a unique, ergonomic shape like a banana or boat curve.
The manual should be user-friendly, avoiding dense text and frequent searching.
nextSteps: Focus on one product design with consistent internal engineering and body shape variations.
Consider a touch-screen interface as a wear-resistant alternative, appealing to younger, office-based users.
Explore low-cost audio or visual cues to help users find the remote and avoid losing it.
Evaluate the feasibility of a free help service for mobile phones in retail outlets, considering contract obligations and cost.
Determine how to address the R_S_I_ issue with repetitive strain from small screen movements.
Email the person if more questions arise, even if not answered directly.
Explore five to six design concepts for the remote, with the most appealing chosen as the common design.
Consider incorporating the company logo into the remote's shell-like design instead of a sea shell motif.
